name: appstore-command-center
description: Self-hosted App Store Connect + AdMob dashboard for iOS solo devs: downloads, unified revenue (ads + in-app & subscriptions, broken down by app and day), reviews, ASO rank, rules-based insights. Daily Vercel cron -> git-as-database -> liquid-glass UI. Zero recurring cost. Next.js 15 + GitHub OAuth.

paragraphs: A private, single-user dashboard that pulls App Store Connect data daily and turns it into a monitoring + growth tool for your own iOS apps. Built to run on Vercel's free tier with zero recurring cost: no database, no LLM bills, no SaaS. Daily Vercel Cron auto-discovers every app on your Apple Developer account, runs five collectors (sales, analytics funnel, reviews, ratings, keyword-rank), and commits the raw data as partitioned JSON into a separate private git repo used as the database. A rules-based intelligence layer surfaces anomalies, funnel leaks, keyword opportunities, and a month-end…

Designed for the case "I run a handful of iOS apps and want one dashboard instead of bouncing between App Store Connect, Sensor Tower, and a spreadsheet." Not a competitor-tracker, not an MMP: just your apps, end-to-end honest.

App Store Connect's web UI is fine for one-off lookups and useless as a daily driver. Real third-party stacks start at \$50-\$200/month and assume you're running an ad budget. This project is the middle path: an opinionated dashboard you self-host on Vercel Hobby for free, that pulls exactly the same numbers Apple gives you, sliced the way you want.
features: Git as DB: serverless-friendly, immune to free-tier pauses, full audit trail, cheap to clone for offline analysis. The price is sequential commits: solved with retry-on-409 backoff.
Per-app parallelization: each app writes disjoint paths, so Promise.all across apps is safe and brings 4-app wall-clock from 60s+ down to 30s.
No LLM dependency: review clustering + weekly digest were dropped to keep operating cost at $0. Reviews are still collected and listed.
Single-user OAuth allowlist: simplest possible auth that's not "no auth". For multi-user, swap the signIn callback for a real ACL.
